sections.h2: Where is Ames, Iowa, and how did the city start?
sections.html:
Ames is in Story County in central Iowa, about 30 miles north of Des Moines. The city sits at roughly 922 feet above sea level.

It began in 1864 as a station stop on the Cedar Rapids and Missouri Railroad. It was named for Oakes Ames, a Massachusetts congressman who helped build the transcontinental railroad, and was founded by Cynthia Olive Duff and the railroad figure John Insley Blair. Ames was incorporated on December 20, 1869, and William West became the first mayor in 1870.

The 2020 census counted 66,427 residents, which made Ames the ninth-most populous city in Iowa. For a seller, the railroad-era street grid near downtown and the newer growth farther out mean very different houses under the same city name.

sections.h2: How much does Iowa State University shape the Ames housing market?
sections.html:
Iowa State University shapes it more than any other single institution. The university was founded in 1856, and fall 2023 enrollment was 30,177 students, roughly half the size of the city's resident population.

Campustown, just south of the campus, is a high-density mixed-use area with student apartments, restaurants and nightlife. Ames Main Street and Old Town are the city's historic districts. Houses near campus often have a history as rentals, and that history comes with paperwork that a seller should know about before accepting an offer.

The university is also the biggest employer by a wide margin:

The Iowa Department of Transportation, USDA and the Ames Community School District also appear on the list of larger employers. Wikipedia notes that Ames had a 1.5% unemployment rate by June 2018. That is an old figure, so treat it as history and not as a current reading.

sections.h2: What are the Ames rental registration rules for a seller?
sections.html:
Any rented property in Ames that is not owner-occupied must be registered with the city's Inspection Division. If you are selling a former or current rental, the registration status is part of the sale.

The city's rental FAQ lays out the parts that matter to a seller:

  • A Letter of Compliance lasts one to four years and cannot be renewed without an inspection.
  • An annual fee based on property type is billed each May and is due within 30 days. The billing period runs July 1 to June 30, and fees continue until the city receives a removal form.
  • When a registered rental sells, the registration transfers and no new inspection is required. The seller tells the Inspection Division who the buyer is, and the buyer registers the property in their own name.
  • A buyer can request a pre-sale inspection by submitting the registration form before purchase. A pre-sale inspection requested without registering carries a $56.10 fee, and it is free if the property is registered.

Owner-occupied means a townhouse, condo or detached home lived in by the owner or a first-degree relative. One roomer, one exchange student, or a live-in nanny or nurse is allowed. More than one of those makes the unit a rental. If a tenant is buying the home on contract, owner-occupied status requires a legally recorded contract with the Story County Recorder.

If you stopped renting the house, ask the Inspection Division to confirm the removal form went through. Otherwise fees keep accruing in your name.

sections.h2: What does Ames weather mean for the house you are selling?
sections.html:
Ames has a humid continental climate with warm summers and cold winters. July is the warmest month and January the coldest.

Average annual precipitation is about 38 inches and average snowfall is about 28 inches. Those figures matter for roofs, gutters, basement drainage and furnace age. A buyer who has to finance with a lender will often get an inspection report that lists exactly these items, and repair requests can slow a conventional sale.

A cash buyer looks at the same condition issues but does not need a lender's sign-off. That is the practical difference for a seller with an older furnace or a worn roof in Ames.

sections.h2: How do schools, buses and the airport affect where Ames sellers find buyers?
sections.html:
Public schools in the city are run by the Ames Community School District. Buyers who want a particular school boundary usually start there, and the district is also one of the larger local employers.

CyRide is the city's bus system, and it is the most-used transit system in Iowa, with over 4.7 million rides in 2024. Houses on or near CyRide routes are easier to rent to students and staff without cars, which is a point a landlord seller can mention to a buyer. Ames Municipal Airport is about one mile southeast of the city.

Ames also has a steady stream of newcomers tied to the university, the hospital and the state and federal offices. Move-in timing often follows the academic calendar, and some sellers choose a fast sale so they do not carry a vacant house through a semester break.

sections.h2: What steps does a cash sale of an Ames house involve?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Ames follows a short sequence: you share the address and condition, we review it, and you receive a written offer you can accept or decline.

  • Send the address, the condition of the roof, furnace and plumbing, and whether the house is owner-occupied or rented.
  • Tell us if it is a registered rental so we can plan around the Inspection Division notice for the sale.
  • If tenants live there, tell us their lease end date.
  • A title company prepares the deed, the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement or its exemption sentence, as Iowa recorders require.
  • The deed is recorded with the Story County Recorder at closing.

If the house has a rental registration, a letter from the Inspection Division confirming status can save a week at closing. If you inherited the house and have not yet opened the estate, mention that too, because the court process comes before any sale.

faqs.q: How many people live in Ames?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 66,427 residents. The city's own page on this site cites the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate of 68,220.

faqs.q: What happens to an Ames rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: It transfers to the buyer without a new inspection. You notify the Inspection Division of the buyer's details, and the buyer registers the property in their own name.

faqs.q: What is the largest employer in Ames?
faqs.a: Iowa State University, with 18,212 employees in 2022 according to Wikipedia's employer list. Mary Greeley Medical Center follows with 1,407.
The Ames Community School District runs the city's public schools.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ames house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not need to fix the roof, furnace or interior before closing. Disclose known problems accurately in the paperwork.
